---
title: "Index label letter clash"
indexes:
  - name: minerals
    title: Index of Minerals
    index-labels:
      symbols: "A"
  - name: fossils
    title: Index of Fossils
    index-labels:
      symbols: "Z"
filters:
  - index
---

Both indexes here name the heading over the entries that file under no letter,
and both write a single capital letter as that name. The difference is what
else each index prints. The first also files a term under `A`, so a reader sees
two groups headed `A` — the entries filing under no letter, and the real `A`
group — and this document draws a report saying so. The second files nothing
under `Z`, so its one `Z` heading is the only one on the page and the report
stays silent. Neither index has its groups merged or reordered: what a `symbols:`
word can change is the heading printed over the non-letter group and nothing
else.

## Minerals {#site-minerals}

A term filing under a letter: [Azurite]{.index index="minerals"}. One filing
under none: [%pyrite]{.index index="minerals"}.

## Fossils {#site-fossils}

A term filing under a letter: [Belemnite]{.index index="fossils"}. One filing
under none: [+trilobite]{.index index="fossils"}.
